title: Loan lifecycle and flows
idea: A Loan's lifecycle is a state machine over ACTIVE, OVERDUE, RETURNED and LOST: each state lists where it may go, and every other move is refused.
points: ACTIVE can become OVERDUE, RETURNED or LOST; RETURNED is final.
A nightly job moves ACTIVE loans past their due date to OVERDUE.
Renewal stays inside ACTIVE and is refused when someone reserved the title.
LOST can still become RETURNED when a paid-for copy turns up.

messages.label: borrow(ISBN-1)
messages.note: The member asks for a title. The service picks a free copy.

messages.label: new Loan, ACTIVE
messages.note: The loan starts ACTIVE with a due date 14 days out.

messages.label: renew(LN-1)
messages.note: Before the due date the member asks for more time.

messages.label: anyone waiting?
messages.note: Renewal is refused if another member reserved this title.

messages.label: no
messages.note: Nobody is waiting, so the due date moves forward once.

messages.label: markOverdueIfLate
messages.note: After the new due date passes, the nightly job moves ACTIVE to OVERDUE.

messages.label: return(CP-1)
messages.note: The member finally brings the copy back to the desk.

messages.label: move(RETURNED)
messages.note: OVERDUE to RETURNED is allowed. The fine is priced from the dates.

messages.label: next waiting?
messages.note: The copy goes to the queue head, or back to the shelf if empty.

code.title: Status enum with rules
code.caption: The allowed moves live in the enum. Loan asks the enum before every change, so no caller can skip a rule.

walk.text: LN-1 renews once; the second renewal hits the limit.
It goes overdue, is returned, then the same copy is scanned again.
LN-2 cannot renew because the title is reserved, then it is lost and found.
An `EnumMap` lists the allowed next states for each state.
`move` is the only way to change status, and it refuses illegal moves.
Renewal checks three rules, then pushes the due date by one loan period.
The nightly job only moves loans that are ACTIVE and past due.

pitfalls: Do not set status with a public setter; one move method must check rules.
Make a repeated return a refused no-op, not a second fine or error page.
Do not model renewal as a state; it changes the due date, not the lifecycle.

quiz.q: What does LoanLifecycle print for the second giveBack() on LN-1?
quiz.why: RETURNED has an empty set of next states, so `canMoveTo` is false and `move` prints the refusal without changing anything.

takeaway: Put allowed transitions in the enum and route every change through one method.

starters: Should OVERDUE be a stored state or computed on read?
How do I handle a lost copy that was already paid for?
Does BookCopy need its own state machine too?
